title: docs(app-shell): cite the chat parts-builder instead of enumerating its key set
body:
Fixes #10019

Clause-②: no — a pending changeset's prose and a source comment. No exported symbol and no key on a published payload moves.

## Premise, re-taken before any edit — three legs, each carrying a control

Base for every reading below: `3ac2de829` (merge-base with `origin/main`).

**Leg 1 — both texts still enumerated the old key set.** Quoted as they stood on the base, not as the card describes them:

- `.changeset/9232-cache-approval-envelope.md`, in its fifth paragraph:
  > In the other direction, `output` is the only carrier that survives API mode's SDK store, because `useObjectChat`'s `aiInitialMessages` rebuilds each part from `{type,toolCallId,toolName,input,output,errorText,state}` and drops every other key; a pending-only turn, the shape that path can actually produce, lands there.
- `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useChatConversation.ts`, in the cache-write comment inside `sanitizeChatMessagesForCache`:
  > `output` is the only carrier that survives API mode's SDK store, because `useObjectChat`'s `aiInitialMessages` rebuilds each part from `{type,toolCallId,toolName,input,output,errorText,state}` and drops every other key, after which `extractToolInvocations` re-derives the id by re-parsing the result.

**Leg 2 — objectui#10017 did land the change that falsifies them.** It is `4dbab84d4`, and it is the last commit that touched `packages/plugin-chatbot/src/useObjectChat.ts`. Read at source rather than inferred: the builder is now `toSdkToolPart`, which switches on the invocation's state and constructs one discriminated part per arm. There is **no single fixed key set** any more — `input` and `output` ride only the arms that have them, `errorText` only the error arm, `approval` only the three approval arms. And the builder's own docblock states the other half in its own words:

> **`toolName` is not copied across.** It is an excess property on a `tool-*` part (only the dynamic-tool arm declares one) AND it is dead on this path.

**Leg 3 — the control: a search that would have found a third site.** Three patterns over all 8205 tracked files (newline-tolerant, so a citation split across comment lines cannot hide): a key-list shape (`toolCallId` within 160 chars of `toolName` plus one more of `input` / `output` / `errorText` / `state`), the prose clause (`drops every other key` / `rebuilds each part`), and any text naming the builder (`aiInitialMessages`). The instrument is demonstrably live — the key-list pattern alone hits 25 files — and it **found both known sites**. Two near-misses were read and cleared, so the card's "there may be more" resolves to **exactly two**:

- `packages/components/src/renderers/form/validationRuleKeys.ts` matches `silently drops every other key` — about react-hook-form's validator key set, a different subject.
- `.changeset/8443-chatbot-runtime-role-fold.md` names `aiInitialMessages`, but enumerates **roles** (`'user' | 'assistant' | 'system'`), not part keys, and `toRuntimeRole` still sits at both arms of that builder, so that changeset is still true.

## The argument is still sound, so this is not a deletion

Walked on today's tree rather than taken from the card. A cache-fallback pending-only turn carries `pendingActionId` and the minted `{ status: 'pending_approval', pendingActionId }` envelope in `output`. Whichever arm `toSdkToolPart` takes for it — the approval arm is skipped because the invocation has no framework `approval` envelope, and `reportUnbackedApprovalState` deliberately stays quiet for a `pendingActionId`, so it lands on `deriveSdkToolPart`'s `output-available` arm — the part that reaches the SDK store carries **`output` and no cache-side key**. So `output` really is the carrier that survives, `extractToolInvocations` really does re-derive the id from it, and both texts keep the point they exist to make. Only the literal list was false.

## Before and after

### 1. `.changeset/9232-cache-approval-envelope.md` — a release note, kept in release-note voice

Before:
> … because `useObjectChat`'s `aiInitialMessages` rebuilds each part from `{type,toolCallId,toolName,input,output,errorText,state}` and drops every other key; …

After:
> … because `useObjectChat`'s `aiInitialMessages` rebuilds each part to the chat runtime's own tool-part shape — which carries `output`, and has no room for a cache-side key like `pendingActionId` — and drops every other key; …

It cites the surface that **owns** the key set instead of restating it (AGENTS.md #9), and it stays followable for a CHANGELOG reader with no repository in front of them: no symbol they cannot resolve, no path, no line address. It also keeps the force of "only carrier", which a bare deletion of the list would have lost — the reader still learns why `output` gets through and the part key does not.

### 2. `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useChatConversation.ts` — a code comment, so it names the owner

Before:
> … rebuilds each part from `{type,toolCallId,toolName,input,output,errorText,state}` and drops every other key, after which `extractToolInvocations` re-derives the id by re-parsing the result.

After:
> … rebuilds each part through `toSdkToolPart`, which constructs the chat runtime's own discriminated tool part — a per-state key set that carries `output` and has no place for a cache-side key — and drops every other key, after which `extractToolInvocations` re-derives the id by re-parsing the result.

A reader here does have the tree, so the citation is a **symbol name** that travels with the thing (AGENTS.md #11) rather than a list that goes stale the next time an arm changes.

## Which gate reads either file — asked, and the answer is mostly "none"

⛔ **No gate reads either text for truth, and no test can go RED on this diff.** Both edits are prose; nothing in the tree evaluates the claim they make. That is precisely the hazard AGENTS.md #9 names, and it is why the repair points at the instrument instead of minting a fresh enumeration.

What does SELECT the files, and on what coordinate:

| gate | selects | what it judges, and what it said here |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `check-changeset-overwrite` | the edited changeset | that a pre-existing declaration was modified. Reported it, named the modification its **legitimate case 2** ("You are CORRECTING a declaration on purpose — … prose that no longer matches the change"), and confirmed `@object-ui/app-shell: patch` is declared both at base and now. Report-only, exit 0 — exactly the behaviour the card predicted. |
| `check:changeset-claims` | the edited changeset, in 2 of its 3 readings | self-contradiction reading: corpus "2 changeset(s) this change adds or modifies, 1 of them declaring a package" → PASS. Born-false reading: corpus "2 body(ies) this change publishes about itself", 0 line addresses → prints "Read, but nothing to judge". Its went-false reading matches backticked **file names**; neither body names a file, so "No pending changeset names a file this change touches". ⇒ the card's statement that this gate cannot see a key enumeration is confirmed by running it. |
| `check-changeset-presence` | the source file | that a `src/` edit in a released package declares a changeset. It went **RED** on the first run, which is what made the second changeset owed (see below). |
| `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-no-major` | both changesets | front matter only. |
| `check-pending-changeset-literals` | the `.changeset/` directory | file **names** against test sources, never a body. |
| `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` | the source file | byte class; and cross-file line addresses this branch ADDS (0 — the new citation is a symbol). |

## A second changeset was owed, and it is here

`check-changeset-presence` reads any edit under a released package's `src/`, comment or not, and a **modified** changeset does not satisfy it — it counts changesets ADDED ("0 changeset(s) added" on the first run, red). So `.changeset/10019-parts-builder-key-set-texts.md` was added with **empty front matter**, the gate's own documented first-class pass, since a comment publishes nothing. The gate now reads: "1 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s) … Every one of them has an EMPTY frontmatter".

## Evidence

Final gate run taken as the last action before the push, on a clean tree at `a201b7899`, `git status` empty and `git diff HEAD` empty:

```
check-changeset-presence            EXIT=0   ✅ 1 changeset declared, empty frontmatter
check-changeset-overwrite           EXIT=0   ⚠️ 1 modified, case 2 (report-only)
check-changeset-claims              EXIT=0   ✅ no pending changeset names a file this change touches
check-changeset-no-major            EXIT=0   ✅
check-changeset-fixed               EXIT=0   ✅
check-pending-changeset-literals    EXIT=0   ✅
check-control-bytes                 EXIT=0   ✅ 8121 tracked text files scanned
check-new-cross-file-line-citations EXIT=0   ✅ 0 new cross-file line citations
```

Package legs (exit codes captured by redirect, never across a pipe; the two heavy ones through the container's shared verify lock, whose VERDICT line is the reading):

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell exec vitest run … useChatConversation.test.ts __tests__/useChatConversation.test.tsx` → **2 files, 58 tests passed**; `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) → `VERDICT command-exit 0`. ⚠️ Its first run was **not** a red gate: it reported `TS2307 Cannot find module '@object-ui/react'` and siblings, i.e. an unbuilt dependency closure. `pnpm turbo run build --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2` (28 tasks, exit 0) was run first and the type-check then passed — the earlier output measured nothing and is reported rather than counted.
- ESLint, narrowed and declared: run on the one lintable file in the diff, `--format json` reporting **1 file linted, 0 errors, 5 pre-existing `react-hooks` warnings** at lines far from the edit. The population is read from `eslint.config.js` itself — every selector it declares is `**/*.{ts,tsx}` / `**/*.tsx` / specific `.ts` paths, so the two markdown files are outside ESLint's population entirely. Invariance: the config enables **no type-aware linting** (`tseslint.configs.recommended`, no `project` / `projectService` in `languageOptions`), so a comment edit in one file cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` run belongs to CI.
- Control-byte self-scan over the three touched files: `grep -naP` for the control class found nothing, in the same command that found a planted U+000B in a probe file — the zero carries its control.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over all three paths: "NOT GOVERNED — 3 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched."

## Acceptance notes

- ⛔ Not filed, noted only: the card's own suggested clause ("rebuilds each part to the chat runtime's own tool-part shape") was taken for the changeset and extended in each text by what that text's reader can use — a runtime-shape description in the release note, the owning symbol in the code comment. No third site exists; the card's "two" is confirmed rather than assumed.
- This PR stays **draft**, carries **no label**, and does not arm auto-merge — the dispatching seat lands it.
